referenceSources.description:
A dark gray 1990 Opel Kadett E 2.0 GSi hatchback is shown from the rear, parked on a paved lot in front of a brick wall. The car’s sporty features include a roof spoiler, mesh alloy wheels, and a prominent exhaust pipe. The Dutch license plate “YT-17-FJ” with an NL country code is clearly visible on the tailgate.

Captured on October 29, 2013, at 16:55 with a SONY DSC camera, the image settings were 1/100 sec exposure, f/4.5 aperture, ISO 400, and a 100 mm lens. The photograph measures 1280 × 1880 pixels at 72 dpi and is available under a Creative Commons license requiring attribution.

SUBJECT: Opel Kadett Gsi, racing preparation referencing Kadett GSi Gruppo A (1988). The photograph measures 1280 × 1880 pixels at 72 dpi and is available under a Creative Commons license requiring attribution.. Use period racing hardware and bodywork rather than generic modern aero. Input3 is PIXEL STYLE/CAMERA ONLY, never borrow the Fiat Punto body. CRITICAL MODEL ANATOMY: Opel Kadett E GSi THREE-DOOR. Rear hatch window is MUCH MORE RAKED: strong diagonal descending roof/glass from the rear roof to short tail, with a thick triangular C-pillar; not a vertical station wagon or upright generic hatch. Very broad single front side door and triangular rear side glass, NO rear door. GSi horizontal rear lip spoiler on hatch lower trailing edge, low horizontal rectangular tail lights. Preserve original white car nose, aero wheel covers and body skirts.. Road-car prohibitions on spoilers, arches or stock wheels are superseded ONLY by the requested racing preparation; retain the actual model identity. REQUIRED VISIBLE PHYSICAL MODIFICATIONS: retain Kadett E steep sloping rear hatch, period rally bumper and flares, hatch spoiler, white compact rally wheels and mud flaps. Do NOT merely recolour the stock sprite: rebuild the listed bumpers, splitter, flares, skirts, wing and competition wheels with believable proportions. The chosen period livery is white yellow and grey Opel racing bands. Keep small sponsor/number panels coherent with period racing; simplify tiny lettering into clean pixel marks without UI text. Where a real race reference is another derivative, preserve the approved road generation, door count and headlight identity; translate the race kit onto the SAME road model, never swap the vehicle. No drivetrain or engine-location change implied by the body. One entire isolated car, front-left three-quarter camera, nose pointing down-left, approximately40%front60%side, straight wheels, realistic body proportions and generous clear margins on a wide3:1 canvas. Transparent background, no cast shadow or ground plane, no scenery, people, multiple views, captions or watermark. STRICT hand-drawn 1990s PC racing game pixel art on a logical320x128 grid: sharp stepped outline, dark one-pixel panel gaps, clean square clusters and compact5-6shade material ramps. No photorealism or photo filter, no3D/vector rendering, antialiasing, smooth gradients, blur, noisy textures, modern giant wheels, modern LED lighting, post-2002 GT3 equipment or mismatched body generations.
